description: Use this when the user wants a calendar file to import, for example "make a calendar file for this meeting", "create an .ics for my weekly class", "export these dates so I can import them". Input tips: pass 1 to 50 events, each with a title, a start (2026-11-02 for all day, or 2026-11-02T09:30) and an end or duration_minutes, plus timezone (IANA name such as Europe/Paris) for a time without Z or an offset; ask the user for the time zone, never guess it. Example event: {"title":"Sprint review","start":"2026-11-02T09:30","duration_minutes":45,"timezone":"Europe/Paris"}. Optional: location, description, reminder_minutes and recurrence (freq daily, weekly, monthly or yearly, with interval, until or count, and byday). Returns: the .ics text, a download link that works for 24 hours, its expiry and the event count. Not for: adding, changing or reading events in Google Calendar, Outlook or any calendar account; it only makes a file. Errors: status invalid with a message naming the event and field to fix.

description.description: Optional notes shown in the event body, such as the agenda.

duration_minutes.description: Length of a timed event in minutes instead of end, such as 45.

end.description: Same format as start, such as 2026-11-02T10:15. For an all-day event it is the last day, inclusive. Give this or duration_minutes.

location.description: Optional place or meeting link shown in the event, such as Room 4B or https://meet.example.com/abc.

recurrence.description: Optional repeat, such as {"freq":"weekly","byday":["MO"],"count":10}. In a zone with daylight saving, give until or count.

byday.description: Weekdays for a weekly repeat, e.g. ["MO","WE"].

count.description: Number of occurrences. Give until or count.

freq.description: How often it repeats: daily, weekly, monthly or yearly.

interval.description: Every N days, weeks, months or years. Default 1.

until.description: Last date of the repeat, such as 2026-12-31. Give until or count, not both.

reminder_minutes.description: Show a reminder this many minutes before the event.

start.description: 2026-11-02 for an all-day event, or 2026-11-02T09:30 (add Z or an offset such as +07:00 if there is no timezone).

timezone.description: IANA time zone name such as America/New_York. Required for a time without Z or an offset.

title.description: Event title, such as Sprint review.

filename.description: File name in letters and digits, such as sprint-review; .ics is added.

name: make_calendar_file

download_url.description: Link that works for 24 hours, or null when no link could be made.

event_count.description: Number of events in the file when status is ok.

expires_at.description: When the link stops working (ISO 8601 UTC).

filename.description: Name the download link saves the file as, such as calendar.ics.

ics_text.description: The whole .ics file (RFC 5545) when status is ok.

message.description: What to fix in the input when status is invalid.

notes.description: Facts the user should know, such as how long the link works.

status.description: ok when the file was made; invalid when the input needs a fix (see message).

title: Make a calendar (.ics) file
